1. [See 
DMG memo 01-26
] This memo gives guidance on The Carer’s Assistance (Carer Support 
Payment) (Scotland) Regulations 2023 (Consequential Amendments) Order 2023
1
 which come into 
force on 19.11.23.

2. This order
1
 makes changes to social security legislation to reflect the introduction of the Carer 
Support Payment (CSP) which replaces CA in Scotland.

3. 
From 19.11.23 a claimant cannot have entitlement to both CA and CSP for the same day
1
. Additionally, 
where two or more people are caring for the same severely disabled person, only one of them will be 
entitled to either CA or CSP for any day. It will be up to them to choose and elect who will be entitled to 
CA or CSP
2
 
by giving the DM a notice in writing signed by both carers specifying who should be entitled 
to CA or CSP
3
. If there is no election t
he Secretary of State should be satisfied that one carer has the 
relevant entitlement to the benefit, following consultation with the Scottish DM
4
.

Note:
 
 
When a DM encounters a rival carer situation, a structured consultation process with the Scottish 
DM’s, carefully considering all the key factors, should take place to ensure that the most appropriate 
carer is chosen.

1 SS CB Act 92, s 70(7); 2 s 70(7ZA), s70(7ZB), s70(7ZC);
3 SS (ICA) Regs, reg 7(1) & 7(1A); 4 SS CB Act 92, s 70(7ZA), s70(7ZB) & s70(7ZC).

Example 1
Mary and Sharon both care for Henry for at least 35 hours a week each. Mary lives in England and claims 
CA. Sharon lives in Scotland and claims CSP. Only one of them will be entitled to benefit for caring for 
Henry. Mary and Sharon decide themselves that Mary should have entitlement. Therefore, Mary receives 
CA. Sharon is not entitled to CSP for the period Mary is entitled to CA.

Example 2
David and Eric both care for Susan for at least 35 hours a week each. David lives in England and claims 
CA. Eric lives in Scotland and claims CSP. Only one of them will be entitled to benefit for caring for Susan. 
David and Eric both believe they should be entitled to claim and cannot decide between them who should 
be entitled. The DM should consult with the Scottish DM to determine which carer has the relevant 
entitlement.
Deferring Entitlement to State Pension/Retirement Pension

4. 
DMG 75405
 et seq provides guidance on people entitled to a lump sum payment when they defer 
their RP. The amount of RP which would have been payable had it not been deferred does 
not 
include 
any pension, where for all of an accrual period, a person has been in receipt of CSP
1
.

5. 
DMG 75349
 et seq provides guidance on people entitled to increments when they defer their RP.
  
DMG 
74501
 et seq
 
 provides guidance on people entitled to increments when they defer their SP. When 
a person is deferring their

they will not be entitled to increments for any day in a period of deferment when they are in receipt of 
Carer Support Payment.

1 
SS (WB & RP) Regs, reg 4(1)(b)(v); 2 SP Regs, reg 11(2)(a)(via)

6. 
DMG 75281
 et seq provides guidance on people entitled to age addition. This will include a person in 
receipt of CSP
1
.

7.
 
 People are entitled to IS if they meet the conditions of entitlement, including where they are in a 
prescribed category
1
 (see 
DMG 20081 et seq
). This includes people who care for another person and are 
entitled to CA
2
. From 19.11.23, the category includes people who care for another person and are entitled 
to CSP
3
.
1 SS C&B Act 92, s 124(1)(e); 2 IS (Gen) Regs, Sch 1B para 4(b);

8. When considering entitlement to any premiums, where there are references to a CA, there shall be a 
reference to a CSP
1
.
Definition of sums to be disregarded

9. From 19.11.23 the definition of sums to be disregarded in the calculation of earnings
1
 will also include a 
CSP carer’s assistance given in accordance with these regulations
2
.

10. The disregard of £20 applied to a carer's earnings where the claimant's applicable amount includes a 
CP and the carer is in receipt of CA also applies where the claimant is in receipt of CSP
1
.

11. Disregard any amount of CSP that is in excess of the amount the claimant would receive if they had an 
entitlement to CA
1
.
Claim for Cat A or Cat B Retirement Pension

12. From 19.11.23 neither a claim to, nor an award of, CSP prevents the Secretary of State from notifying 
the beneficiary that a claim for Cat A or Cat B RP is not required
1
.

13. 
DMG 20902-DMG 20903
 
gives guidance on when a JSA claimant or a joint-claim couple do not have 
to serve waiting days, including where entitlement to JSA begins within 12 weeks of the end of 
entitlement to specified benefits
1
. From 19.11.23, CSP
2
 
is added to the list of qualifying benefits.

1
 
JSA Regs, reg 46(1)(a) & (d)
; 2
 
CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23

14. 
DMG 21027
 gives guidance on linked periods. From 19.11.23 a linked period will include when
 
a 
claimant is entitled to a CSP
1
.
Carers, remunerative work and joint claimants

15.
 
 For the purpose of whether a JSA claimant is

1. 
in remunerative work where they are a carer
1
 
(see 
DMG 20252
) 
or

2.
 a member of a joint claim couple who does not have to satisfy the conditions of entitlement
2
 
because 
they are a carer
3
 
(see
 
DMG 20017
).

CSP
4
 is added to the list of qualifying benefits from 19.11.23. See
 
Chapter 20
 
(JSA conditions of 
entitlement) for further details.
1 JSA Regs, reg 51(3)(c)(iii); 2 JS Act 95, s 1(2B)(b);

3 JSA Regs, Sch A1, para 3(b); 4 
CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23

16. When considering entitlement to any premiums, where there are references to a CA, there shall be a 
reference to a CSP
1
.
Definition of sums to be disregarded in the calculation of earnings

17. From 19.11.23 the sums to be disregarded in the calculation of earnings
1
 will also include a CSP carer’s 
assistance given in accordance with these regulations
2
.

1 JSA Regs, Sch 6 para 7; 2
   
CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23

18. The disregard of £20 applied to a carer's earnings where the claimant's applicable amount includes a 
CP and the carer is in receipt of CA also applies where the claimant is in receipt of CSP
1
.
1 JSA Regs, Sch 6, para 7; Sch 6A, para 2
Definition of sums to be disregarded in the calculation of income other than earnings

19. From 19.11.23 the sums to be disregarded in the calculation of income other than earnings
1
 will also 
include a CSP carer’s assistance given in accordance with these regulations
2
.

1 JSA Regs, Sch 6 para 7; 2 
CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23

20. From 19.11.23 disregard any amount of CSP that is in excess of the amount the claimant would 
receive if they had an entitlement to CA
1
.
Change of circumstances supersession where award of CSP ends

21. From 19.11.23 the definition of date from which a decision superseded under section 10 takes effect
1
 
will also include a CSP carer’s assistance given in accordance with these regulations
2
.

1 SS CS (D&A) regs, reg 7(2)(bc); 2 
CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23

1.
 the claimant is a disabled person or a disabled person’s partner 
and

2.
 a decision awarding benefit is superseded to the claimant's advantage 
and

3.
 the reason for the supersession is that payment of an award of CSP in respect of that disabled person 
has ended

the superseding decision is effective from the day after the last day that CSP was paid to a person other 
than the claimant or the claimant’s partner
1
. 
DMG 02010
 (main heading) and 
DMG 04226
 are affected.

23. CSP is a social security benefit and is taken into account as income other than earnings
1. 
Disregard 
any amount of CSP that is in excess of the amount the claimant would receive if they had an entitlement 
to CA
2
.
1 SPC Regs, reg 15(1); 2 SPC Regs, Sch IV, para 19

24.
 
 DMG
 
85447
 
explains that where a claimant to whom 
DMG 85441
 applies is in receipt of an 
overlapping benefit or allowance the amount of RP income they shall be treated as having is the RP they 
are entitled to minus the amount of the benefit or allowance in payment
1
. From 19.11.23 CSP is included 
as such an overlapping benefit or allowance
2
.

1
 
SPC Regs, reg 18(1CA)
; 2 
CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23
Additional amount for the severely disabled

25. 
DMG 78030
 and
 78610
 gives guidance that when considering entitlement to an additional amount 
for claimants who are severely disabled, no amount is payable in respect of a claimant if someone is in 
receipt of

in respect of caring for them
1
. From 19.11.23 CSP is included in the list of qualifying benefits
2
.

1 
SPC regs, Sch I para1(1)
 
&
 
Sch III para 1(10)(d)
; 
 
2
   
CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23

26. 
DMG 78100
 and 
78620
 gives guidance that an additional amount for carers may be awarded for 
each claimant who is entitled to CA. From 19.11.23 that also includes those claimants entitled to CSP
1
.

27. 
DMG 39408
 and 
Appendix 6 to DMG Chapter 39
 gives guidance on arrears of benefits payable to the 
deceased not being counted as assets of the deceased when considering deductions from the amount 
of award of funeral payment. From 19.11.23 arrears of CSP payable to the deceased as at the date of 
death are excluded from the assets of the deceased
1

28.
 
 
DMG 41032
 gives guidance on relaxation of the first contribution condition
1
 where specified 
conditions are met, including where the ESA claimant is entitled to CA in the last complete tax year 
immediately before the relevant benefit year in which the first day of LCW occurred
2
. From 19.11.23 this 
includes where the claimant is entitled to CSP
3
.

1 WR Act 07, Sch 1, Part 1, para 1(4)(b);
 
2 ESA Regs, reg 8(2)(a);

29.
 
 
DMG 41103
 gives guidance on when an ESA claimant does not have to serve waiting days, including 
where entitlement to ESA begins within 12 weeks of the end of entitlement to specified benefits
1
. From 
19.11.23, CSP
2
 is added to the list of qualifying benefits.

1 ESA Regs, reg 144(2)(a); 2
 CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23

30. From 19.11.23 the amounts
1
 will also include a CSP carer’s assistance given in accordance with these 
regulations
2
.

1 ESA Regs, Sch 42;
 
CA (CSP)(Scot) Regs 23(CA) Order 23
Amount of ESA payable where entitlement is for less than a week

31. When calculating the amount of ESA payable, where there are references to a CA, there shall be a 
reference to a CSP
1
.

Note:
 
See guidance at 
DMG 46072
,
 
46121
,
 
46062
, 
46092
 and 
46112
.

32. 
When considering entitlement to any premiums, where there are references to a CA, there shall be a 
reference to a CSP
1
.

33. From 19.11.23 disregard any amount of CSP that is in excess of the amount the claimant would 
receive if they had an entitlement to CA
1
.
State Pension, Retirement Pension and Widowed Parent’s Allowance
Additional Pension and Engaged in Caring

34. 
DMG 75549
 et seq and 
63062
 et seq provides guidance
 
that a person who is engaged in caring
 
can 
receive a class 3 credit
 
towards satisfying the single contribution condition. This will include a person 
engaged in caring for a period of up to 12 weeks,

1. 
before they become entitled to CSP
1 
or

2
. after they cease to be entitled to CSP
2

However,
 
2.
 
does not apply if a claimant continues to be entitled to a credit after entitlement to CSP 
ends
3
.
1 SS (CC P & C) Regs, reg 7(1)(a); 2 reg 7(1)(b); 3 reg 7(2)
Additional Pension and Applications for NI credits

35. 
See DMG 75556
 and 
63069
 for guidance on applications for NI credits when engaged in caring. 
NI 
credits cannot be awarded in respect of claims to CSP, or the Carer Credit, for any period where the 
person was a married woman who had elected to pay a reduced rate of NI contributions (Married 
Woman's Reduced Rate Election)
1
.
